mstts:express-as.prosody: Welcome to this journey. If you’ve ever found yourself wide awake in the middle of the night, holding a tiny, squirming bundle and wondering how you’ll ever get through the next hour—let alone the next year—you’re not alone. That first year with a newborn? It’s a rollercoaster. There are sleepless nights, moments when you feel completely exposed, and then—right in the middle of it all—unexpected sparks of pure joy. Together, we’ll step into the world Anne Lamott so bravely shares in "Operating Instructions: A Journal of My Son’s First Year." Her story isn’t just about surviving new motherhood; it’s about navigating every tangled emotion, every wave of doubt, and every surge of fierce, protective love that comes with bringing a new life into the world. What’s so powerful about her journey is how it reflects all our hidden fears and hopes, especially when she faces raising her child alone—balancing personal worries and that ever-present sense of uncertainty. Through Anne’s eyes, the daily grind of caring for a newborn becomes something bigger—a lens that helps us see the messy, beautiful layers of life, faith, and resilience. As we move through her days, we’ll witness how each challenge and tiny victory shapes the growing bond between mother and son. It’s a story woven with laughter, frustration, and those moments of tenderness that just stop you in your tracks. Through her candid, unfiltered reflections, Anne Lamott invites us to look closer at the chaos and exhaustion of parenthood—and find a place of acceptance, hope, and gratitude. So, let’s explore together what it truly means to care for someone else, while still learning to care for ourselves.
